content.user_title: Diagnose Context Degradation in AI Systems
content.value_statement: Long conversations and overloaded prompts can reduce model accuracy in ways that are difficult to diagnose. This skill identifies degradation patterns and recommends practical context management strategies.
actual_capabilities: Explains lost-in-middle, context poisoning, distraction, confusion, and clash.
Maps common agent symptoms to likely context degradation patterns.
Recommends write, select, compress, and isolate strategies.
Suggests context placement, filtering, segmentation, and compaction techniques.
Provides guidance for testing performance across increasing context lengths.
limitations: Does not measure context length or model performance automatically.
Model thresholds are illustrative and may change as models evolve.
Research claims do not include direct source links.
Reliable diagnosis still requires application logs, evaluations, and environment-specific testing.

use_cases.title: Debug a Long Agent Session
use_cases.description: Identify why an agent forgets requirements, repeats errors, or selects irrelevant tools after many turns.

use_cases.title: Design Context Evaluations
use_cases.description: Create tests that vary context length, information placement, distractors, and conflicting sources.

use_cases.title: Improve Prompt Architecture
use_cases.description: Choose filtering, compaction, retrieval, or task isolation based on the observed failure pattern.

prompt_templates.title: Identify the Failure Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this agent behavior: [behavior]. Classify the likely context degradation pattern and explain the evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when an agent begins producing weaker answers during a long session.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Context Placement
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this prompt structure: [structure]. Reorder critical information to reduce lost-in-middle risk while preserving all requirements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when important instructions are buried inside a large prompt.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Mitigation Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this workflow: [workflow]. Compare write, select, compress, and isolate strategies, then recommend an implementation with tradeoffs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when designing a reliable long-running agent.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Degradation Evaluation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an evaluation plan for [system]. Test context length, placement, distractors, poisoning, and conflicting sources. Define metrics, thresholds, and recovery checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when validating a production AI system under context pressure.

output_examples.input: The agent follows an outdated requirement even after the user corrects it.
output_examples.output: Likely pattern: context poisoning or clash. Remove the outdated requirement, mark the correction as authoritative, and retest from a clean checkpoint.

output_examples.input: A model misses a key constraint buried between several long documents.
output_examples.output: Likely pattern: lost in the middle. Move the constraint near the beginning and restate it in a concise final checklist.

output_examples.input: A support agent uses policies from an unrelated product.
output_examples.output: Likely pattern: context confusion. Separate product contexts, filter retrieved policies by product, and expose only tools relevant to the active task.

best_practices: Measure task quality as context grows instead of relying on advertised window size.
Keep verified goals and critical constraints near attention-favored positions.
Filter, version, and label retrieved information before adding it to context.
anti_patterns: Do not load every available document without relevance filtering.
Do not preserve incorrect summaries after evidence changes.
Do not mix unrelated tasks, tool definitions, and policies in one context.

faq.question: What is context degradation?
faq.answer: It is a gradual decline in model reliability as context becomes longer, noisier, contradictory, or incorrectly summarized.

faq.question: What does lost in the middle mean?
faq.answer: Models often recall information near the beginning and end better than information placed in the middle.

faq.question: How is context poisoning different from context clash?
faq.answer: Poisoning propagates incorrect information. Clash occurs when multiple context items conflict, even when each item may be valid in another setting.

faq.question: Does a larger context window prevent degradation?
faq.answer: No. Capacity does not guarantee consistent retrieval, reasoning, or instruction adherence across the entire window.

faq.question: Which mitigation should I try first?
faq.answer: Start by removing irrelevant content and surfacing current goals. Add compaction or task isolation when the context continues growing.

faq.question: Can this skill test my system automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides diagnostic and evaluation guidance, but you must run measurements with your model, prompts, tools, and data.
